# Edge Cases and Pathological Input

This file feeds the viewer degenerate, malicious and oversized input: empty and huge headings, 50 thematic breaks in a row, block quotes nested 30 levels deep, deeply nested emphasis and brackets, dangerous URLs (`javascript:`, `data:`, `file://`), Windows and UNC paths full of backslashes, invalid character references, 10,000-character lines, stray whitespace and TABs, and constructs that are never closed. **The file uses CRLF (`\r\n`) line endings on purpose**, with a few bare-LF and bare-CR lines mixed in. It was generated by `tools/gen_edge_cases.py`. The viewer must not crash, hang, execute anything, or show stray `\r` glyphs. It ends with an unclosed code fence (and no final newline), which must run to the end of the document.

## Line endings

Every line in this file ends with CRLF, except for the marked lines below. A hard line break made with two trailing spaces or with a backslash must still work when CRLF follows it:

Two trailing spaces before CRLF  
gives a hard break here.

A backslash before CRLF\
gives a hard break here too.

The next paragraph mixes line endings: its first line ends with a bare LF and its second with a bare CR. It must still read as one paragraph of three lines joined by soft breaks:

This line ends with a bare LF,
this line ends with a bare CR (classic Mac OS),and this line ends with CRLF again.

## Dangerous and unusual URLs

Nothing in this section may execute script, open a program, or fetch a local file without the user's consent. The safe outcome is to show these as inert links or text, or not render them. cmark-gfm's safe mode, for example, replaces `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `file:` and non-image `data:` URLs with an empty href.

- Empty source: ![empty src]() and ![empty angle src](<>) and <img src="" alt="html empty src">
- `javascript:` source: ![js image](javascript:alert('img')) and <img src="javascript:alert(1)" alt="html js src">
- `onerror` handler: <img src="img/does-not-exist.png" onerror="alert('onerror')" alt="onerror handler">

## Windows paths and backslashes

A backslash is only an escape before ASCII punctuation, and a backslash is itself punctuation. So `\\` turns into **one** backslash in normal text, while `\P` stays as typed.

- Program Files: C:\Program Files\Total Commander\TOTALCMD64.EXE (backslashes before letters stay)
- Double backslashes in text: C:\\Windows\\System32 (expected: single backslashes, because each `\\` is an escape)
- UNC path in text: \\server\share\folder\file.md (expected: **one** leading backslash)
- UNC path in code: `\\server\share\folder\file.md` (expected: two leading backslashes)
- A path whose backslash ends the paragraph stays literal (a hard break can't end a block): C:\Temp\
- Backslash before `*`: C:\*.md shows `C:*.md`, and the star is escaped
- Registry: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Ghisler\Total Commander (underscores inside words stay literal)
- [Link with a Windows path](C:\Users\Public\Documents\readme.md)
- [Relative link with backslashes](..\sample-readme.md)
- [UNC link](\\server\share\doc.md) (the destination starts with a single backslash after escaping)
- <a href="file:///C:/Projects/mdview-wlx/README.md">HTML file:/// link to the repository README</a>

```bat
rem In a code block every backslash is literal:
copy "C:\Program Files\Total Commander\wincmd.ini" "\\backup-server\configs\tc\"
dir \\?\C:\Very\Long\Path\Prefix\ /s
```

## Character references

| Source | Result | Why |
|--------|--------|-----|
| `&#0;` | &#0; | NUL is replaced with U+FFFD |
| `&#xD800;` | &#xD800; | a lone surrogate becomes U+FFFD |
| `&#x110000;` | &#x110000; | beyond U+10FFFF: U+FFFD (or literal, depending on digit count) |
| `&#xFFFFFFFF;` | &#xFFFFFFFF; | 8 hex digits, more than the spec's 6: literal per spec |
| `&#99999999;` | &#99999999; | 8 decimal digits, more than the spec's 7: literal per spec (cmark-gfm prints U+FFFD) |
| `&#65;` `&#x41;` | &#65; &#x41; | both are the letter A |
| `&foo;` | &foo; | unknown name: literal |
| `&amp` | &amp | no semicolon: literal |
| `&AMP;` | &AMP; | valid HTML5 name: & |
| `&Amp;` | &Amp; | wrong case: literal |
| `&#;` `&#x;` | &#; &#x; | no digits: literal |
| `&#x1F600;` | &#x1F600; | 😀 |
| `&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;` | [&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;] | three no-break spaces |
| `&#42;&#42;x&#42;&#42;` | &#42;&#42;x&#42;&#42; | entities never create markup: literal `**x**` |

---

## Control characters

Each character sits between brackets. A viewer should show nothing, a replacement glyph, or a visible control picture, but never break the layout:

- SOH U+0001: [], BEL U+0007: [], BS U+0008: [], VT U+000B: [], FF U+000C: []
- ESC U+001B: [] and an ANSI color sequence: [[31mred?[0m]
- DEL U+007F: [], NEL U+0085: []
- LINE SEPARATOR U+2028: [ ] and PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR U+2029: [ ] (these are not line endings in Markdown)
- Noncharacters U+FFFE: [￾] and U+FFFF: [￿], replacement character U+FFFD: [�]
- A private-use character U+E000: [], and plane-15 PUA U+F0000: [󰀀]

## Whitespace and TABs

Words	separated	by	TABs	in	a	paragraph render like spaces.

-	A list item whose marker is followed by a TAB
-	Another one

#	Heading after a TAB (valid ATX heading)

| TAB	in	cell | x |
|---|---|
| a	b | c	d |

A line with trailing TABs is not a hard break:		
so this continues the same line.

A line with one trailing space is not a hard break: 
so this continues the same line.

A line that ends with two spaces and then a TAB  	
is a soft break in cmark-gfm, because the character right before the line ending is a TAB, not a space.

The next line holds only spaces and TABs, which makes it blank:

 	  	 
This paragraph follows a whitespace-only line.

	A TAB-indented line after a blank line is an indented code block.

   Three leading spaces: a normal paragraph.

Unicode spaces at line start (U+3000 and U+00A0) are **not** indentation:

　　Ideographic spaces at the start of this paragraph.

    Four no-break spaces: still a paragraph, not code.

## Unclosed constructs

These are the last items in the file, because each can swallow whatever follows it.

**An HTML table that is never closed.** Markdown ends the HTML block at the next blank line, but an HTML engine may keep the table open:

<table><tr><td>cell in an unclosed table

**A `<div align="center">` that is never closed.** On github.com, the browser may center *everything* below this point:

<div align="center">

Centered text inside an unclosed div.

**A `<details>` that is never closed.** On github.com, everything below this point may end up inside the collapsed block:

<details>
<summary>Unclosed details (click to expand)</summary>

Content inside the unclosed details block.

**A code fence that is never closed.** The fenced block runs to the end of the document, and everything in it, including the Markdown-looking lines, must render as code:

```python
def never_closed():
    return 'this fence has no closing line'

# This looks like a heading, but it is code.
**not bold**, [not a link](https://example.com), <!-- not a comment
> not a quote
| not | a | table |
|-----|---|-------|

The document ends here, without a closing fence and without a final newline.
